Scale-free collective correlations make the susceptibility grow with system size according to a critical power.

change_summary: Added a subleading finite-size correction term to the critical susceptibility law. This produces scale-dependent curvature in log-log plots and a drifting effective exponent before the asymptotic pure power law is recovered.

add_term_audit.mechanism_claim: A leading irrelevant scaling field adds a subleading susceptibility contribution at criticality that competes with the asymptotic power law over moderate system sizes.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed critical temperature and zero field, susceptibility is a pure power law chi(L)=susceptibility_amplitude*L**critical_exponent_ratio with constant log-log slope critical_exponent_ratio.
response_change.child_relation: Add the leading finite-size correction from an irrelevant scaling field so chi(L) keeps the asymptotic power law but acquires scale-dependent curvature in log-log coordinates, with the effective slope drifting toward the asymptotic exponent as L increases.
response_change.observable_effect: Across small-to-moderate versus large system sizes, the apparent exponent extracted from local log-log slopes changes systematically; one shared pure-power parent fit cannot reproduce this size-dependent bending while also matching the large-L asymptote.

evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate and large sizes can already show a gentle log-log bend away from a single straight line; in holdout at larger L the same mechanism predicts approach back toward the parent power law rather than a new phase or threshold.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law by sending the correction amplitude to zero or by taking L to asymptotically large values so the irrelevant-field contribution vanishes.

evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: At criticality, irrelevant renormalization-group fields generate subleading finite-size contributions that modify the amplitude in an L-dependent way while preserving the same asymptotic exponent ratio.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: The added subleading power competes with the leading scaling contribution over accessible sizes, creating a drifting local exponent rather than a single global gain. evolution_contract.assumption_before: The parent assumes finite-size critical susceptibility is an exact single power of L over the entire sampled size range, with no preasymptotic correction.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Finite sizes receive a competing subleading contribution from the leading irrelevant field, so the asymptotic power law is approached gradually rather than holding exactly at all sampled L.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: correction_amplitude -> 0, or L -> infinity with correction_exponent > 0
evolution_contract.observable_signature: At fixed critical conditions, moderate sizes exhibit a bent log-log chi versus L relation with local slope drifting toward critical_exponent_ratio as L increases; the parent predicts no such slope drift.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of susceptibility_amplitude and critical_exponent_ratio can only produce one constant log-log slope across all L. It cannot simultaneously match curvature at moderate sizes and the large-L asymptotic slope with one shared parameter set unless the correction term is negligible over the whole sampled range.

derivation_notes: The parent assumes one irrelevant scaling field controls all observable finite-size deviations. Here that assumption is relaxed by allowing an additional subleading correction whose visibility is limited to a finite preasymptotic size window, representing secondary irrelevant or analytic contributions while preserving the same large-L critical asymptote.
change_summary: Added a subleading correction-to-scaling channel with finite-size saturation so chi(L) can show extra log-log curvature across moderate sizes before returning to the asymptotic critical power. This changes the target mapping itself, not just hidden auxiliary structure.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The leading finite-size correction alone captures the observable departure from asymptotic critical scaling across the sampled system sizes.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Multiple irrelevant renormalization-group fields or analytic finite-size contributions generate an additional subleading correction-to-scaling term at criticality, but its visibility is itself limited to a finite preasymptotic size regime.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Recover the parent law by taking the added subleading correction amplitude to zero or by sending its exponent sufficiently large that its contribution is negligible over the sampled L range.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed critical temperature, chi is a sum of two pure powers of L, so the log-log slope drifts monotonically toward critical_exponent_ratio with only one leading correction scale.
response_change.child_relation: Keep the same critical-point finite-size setting but relax the assumption that one irrelevant field dominates over the sampled sizes; include a second subleading correction so the effective log-log slope shows additional curvature before reaching the asymptotic exponent.
response_change.observable_effect: Across increasing L at fixed geometry, boundary conditions, couplings, and temperature, the child can produce a two-stage approach of the effective exponent versus 1/L-scale, whereas the parent only allows a single-stage monotonic drift tied to one correction exponent.

evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the added contribution is not just another unrestricted pure power: it is active mainly in a finite size window through an explicit crossover denominator, creating extra curvature that cannot be reproduced by rescaling existing amplitudes and one correction exponent alone.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: A single dominant irrelevant field controls all observable finite-size deviations throughout the sampled critical scaling window.

Retuning susceptibility_amplitude, critical_exponent_ratio, correction_amplitude, and correction_exponent can shift that one crossover but cannot generate the added finite-size-limited curvature regime produced by the extra subleading correction.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when sampled sizes span at least roughly one to several decades and the universality class or effective dimensional setting is near a marginal case where logarithmic finite-size corrections are expected; over a narrow L window the effect may be too weak to distinguish from ordinary algebraic corrections.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate sizes show gentle but persistent excess curvature beyond the parent's algebraic-plus-saturation form; in holdout at larger L, the same mechanism continues as a slow logarithmic drift instead of saturating away, extending the mismatch.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit that the logarithmic correction amplitude tends to zero, or over a restricted size window where log factors are nearly constant and can be approximated by refitted amplitudes.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The parent assumes every visible finite-size correction is algebraic in L, with one subleading contribution further turned off by a finite crossover scale; it omits marginally irrelevant scaling fields that generate logarithmic finite-size renormalization at criticality.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: All correction-to-scaling structure at the fixed critical point is representable by ordinary power laws in L, optionally suppressed by a finite crossover denominator.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: A marginal or near-marginal irrelevant field modifies the critical finite-size susceptibility through multiplicative or additive logarithmic corrections, causing a slow scale dependence of the effective amplitude/exponent.
evolution_plan.rationale: Vary L while holding geometry, boundary conditions, microscopic couplings, zero field, and the tuned critical temperature fixed. The parent maps size to susceptibility using a dominant critical power plus algebraic corrections, including a subleading branch that eventually saturates away beyond a crossover size. A realistic next refinement is to relax the assumption that the extra curvature must come from a finite crossover suppression: in marginal cases, the target mapping itself acquires slow logarithmic size dependence. The observable contrast is that the parent predicts correction curvature that can be absorbed into algebraic powers and then dies off with increasing L, whereas the child predicts a continuing log-driven drift of the effective slope over larger sizes. This is scientifically admissible near upper critical dimension or when a marginally irrelevant operator is present. The change affects the scored chi(L) relation directly, not merely an auxiliary trajectory. A single refitted parent parameter set may mimic a short interval, but across admissible broad size ranges it cannot simultaneously reproduce both the early and late slow logarithmic drift if the true correction does not saturate to a pure algebraic form.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Make the coefficient of an existing process depend on a declared quantity.

scenario_text: A finite equilibrium system is tuned to the critical temperature of a continuous thermal phase transition. Systems of different linear sizes are sampled while geometry, boundary conditions, and microscopic couplings are fixed. The target is the zero-field susceptibility inferred from equilibrium order-parameter fluctuations. Scale-free collective correlations make the susceptibility grow with system size according to a critical power.

response_change.parent_relation: At one fixed critical environment, chi(L) is a sum of power-law finite-size terms, so log-chi versus log-L approaches a size-independent asymptotic slope with only algebraic correction curvature.
response_change.child_relation: Keep the critical power-law core but replace the sharply saturating subleading suppression by a smooth logarithmic renormalization of the effective amplitude, producing additional slow curvature in chi(L) across decades of L at the upper critical dimension or in marginally irrelevant cases.
response_change.observable_effect: Across a broad size window, the child shows a systematic slow drift of the local effective exponent with log L that cannot be matched by the parent's finite sum of algebraic corrections using one shared parameter set when the data exhibit marginal curvature rather than a simple crossover cutoff.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.leading_logarithmic_amplitude: modest magnitude, typically Abs(leading_logarithmic_amplitude) < 1 so the leading amplitude stays positive over the sampled L range
new_symbol_range_suggestions.leading_logarithmic_strength: positive or modestly negative with 1 + leading_logarithmic_strength * log(1 + (L / leading_logarithmic_crossover_size)**leading_logarithmic_sharpness) remaining positive over sampled L; typically small in magnitude for slow marginal drift

derivation_notes: The parent assumed the dominant critical term was an exact power law in L. Relaxing that assumption, a marginally irrelevant operator is allowed to renormalize the leading scaling field itself through a slowly varying, saturating logarithmic factor, preserving the original law when the new logarithmic amplitude vanishes or the crossover lies outside the sampled range.
change_summary: The leading susceptibility contribution is no longer a pure power law with fixed amplitude; it now carries a saturating logarithmic running motivated by marginal critical scaling. This changes the large-L effective slope of chi(L) in a way that persists after ordinary additive power corrections are refit.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The leading critical finite-size susceptibility contribution is modeled as susceptibility_amplitude * L**critical_exponent_ratio with no marginal logarithmic renormalization of its own.
assumption_audit.mechanism: A marginally irrelevant operator at criticality can renormalize the leading scaling field, producing multiplicative logarithmic corrections to the dominant susceptibility scaling rather than only to a subleading amplitude.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when leading_logarithmic_amplitude = 0, or approximately when leading_logarithmic_crossover_size is far beyond the sampled L range so the new factor is effectively constant and can be absorbed into susceptibility_amplitude.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed critical temperature, chi(L) is a sum of pure power-law finite-size terms with one logarithmically renormalized amplitude, so the large-L effective slope approaches critical_exponent_ratio with only additive inverse-power corrections.
response_change.child_relation: Keep the same critical finite-size structure but relax the assumption that the leading critical contribution is a pure power law; a marginally irrelevant field can multiply the leading term itself by a slow logarithmic factor, changing the L-dependence of the effective slope across decades.
response_change.observable_effect: When L is varied over sufficiently wide decades, the local log-log slope of chi versus L drifts systematically even after subleading power corrections are refit; the drift persists into the largest-L regime rather than dying as a simple additive correction.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes the extra subleading finite-size correction has a fixed algebraic exponent with only a simple denominator suppression, omitting the realistic case that a marginally irrelevant field can renormalize that correction multiplicatively and therefore alter its effective exponent drift with size.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The additional subleading correction-to-scaling contribution is a pure power law in L apart from a saturating amplitude factor, with no logarithmic running in its own scaling dimension.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: A marginal or near-marginal irrelevant operator can mix with a subleading irrelevant scaling field, causing the subleading susceptibility correction to acquire multiplicative logarithmic renormalization and hence a slowly varying effective decay exponent.
evolution_plan.rationale: Vary L while holding the bath temperature at the critical point, geometry, boundary conditions, and microscopic couplings fixed. The parent mapping gives one leading critical growth law plus fixed-exponent corrections whose amplitudes run slowly. That means once parameters are globally fit, the local log-log slope can only approach the asymptote through the specific combination of fixed powers already present. A natural refinement is to relax the idealization that the subleading correction's exponent is fixed: in marginal cases, operator mixing makes that correction decay with an extra logarithmic factor, changing curvature in the target mapping chi(L), not merely an auxiliary quantity. The contrast is observable when the subleading term is still measurable and its logarithmic running has turned on, producing a slower, scale-dependent approach than a single shared parent parameter set can reproduce across small-to-intermediate and larger L simultaneously. This stays within the same zero-field equilibrium critical scenario, preserves positivity/finite-size finiteness when parameters are chosen admissibly, and has a clear parent-recovery limit if the added marginal running is switched off.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Use a finite-capacity, saturation, threshold, or regime-transition response.

scenario_text: A finite equilibrium system is tuned to the critical temperature of a continuous thermal phase transition. Systems of different linear sizes are sampled while geometry, boundary conditions, and microscopic couplings are fixed. The target is the zero-field susceptibility inferred from equilibrium order-parameter fluctuations. Scale-free collective correlations make the susceptibility grow with system size according to a critical power.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed critical temperature, chi(L) is modeled as a pure sum of power-law finite-size terms with logarithmically renormalized amplitudes, so all nonanalytic size dependence is forced into amplitudes while the effective correction exponents remain fixed.
response_change.child_relation: Retain the same critical leading sector but relax the assumption that the additional analytic/irrelevant correction is a pure power with fixed exponent; instead allow the subleading correction itself to acquire multiplicative logarithmic running, changing how its local slope versus log L bends across intermediate and large sizes.
response_change.observable_effect: Across increasing L, the subleading tail shows a slower crossover in effective exponent than any fixed-exponent parent term can mimic with one shared parameter set, producing a distinct drift in d log chi / d log L at sizes where the correction is still visible but the leading term already dominates.

activation_condition: Observable when L is large enough that log(1 + (L / subleading_crossover_size)**subleading_saturation_sharpness) is O(1) or larger, yet not so large that the subleading correction is numerically negligible compared with the leading critical term; this is the intermediate-to-large finite-size regime near the crossover into marginal running.

dependent_variable.description: Finite-system equilibrium susceptibility of the order parameter at the fixed critical temperature

independent_variables.description: Linear system size in microscopic length units

parameters.description: Positive nonuniversal susceptibility amplitude at criticality
Critical exponent ratio gamma/nu, equivalently 2 - eta

Positive exponent of the additional subleading correction-to-scaling contribution

Amplitude of the marginal logarithmic renormalization acting on the leading critical susceptibility sector
Strength controlling how strongly the leading logarithmic factor runs with system size through the logarithm denominator
Crossover size at which the leading marginal logarithmic renormalization becomes observable
Positive sharpness governing the onset saturation of the leading logarithmic renormalization
